content.content:
== Four Months for a Boat (completed)
- Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers asked me to end Rows-For-Another's Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate: eleven years for one holed boat. She gave me a leaf in her own hand to leave in the count-box for the real one, five lockpicks, and 100 gold, the Owing's first price. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the farm.
- Rows-For-Another told me what holds her: her leaf in the count-box inside the estate house, whose key the keeper Hulm-Tei wears; Hulm-Tei's word, which could close the Owing; and Brings-Them-Back, the fetcher on the channel north of the bank, who knows the way to her home tree. I'm to break any one of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back where the channel runs on north of the bank. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now, to fetch her back from it. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
- I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
- I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home, and her Owing will be written onto the keeper. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how. She said to come back to her for more work.
== One Out of the Smoke (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to the stone house on Blackrose's east shore, where the heirs of the Rose, the old prison a day south, keep three of their held. One of the three can be got out. She wants the one held for words, not the one held for a killing. I'm to speak to Third-Born Tsaxi, who keeps the post.
- I killed Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' post. Nobody is left to keep the three, so any of them can go, or all of them. I'm to tell them.
- I told Mends-Nets to go when I had gone. The other two stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
- I told Never-Sold that Mends-Nets came out. Walks-Far stays to work his three seasons, and Seven-Floods stays far from her Hist. Never-Sold said we will be called the people who loose killers, and that it will be true. She paid me 150 gold and said to come back to her for more work.

content.content:
Never-Sold: "Ussa-Rekh, the Broker, bought hundreds of people out of their Owings on Soulrest's dock, on the coast road a short way east of Lilmoth, and now he hires them out, and each freed person's carved token stays in his chest until they have worked a season for him. Heavy-Rope's crew have worked theirs and one more, and I want their tokens in their hands. There is also a bound book on his shelf with my name on it, and I want that too. The tokens lie in his chest in his house, the north house of Soulrest. The key is on his belt, and Feldril Nethri keeps the door. You have three ways in. You can lift the key and open the chest. You can talk Feldril Nethri into leaving the door unbarred, or the old man himself into letting the crew go. Or you can go to the berth-master, the man who finds hands for the boats and pays their hire. Heavy-Rope stands at the head of the dock, and he has the plan. Hear it, and better it if you can. Know what each way costs. The old man sits in his room by the chest, so every way through that house is under his eye, and seen, you are a thief. And remember what he is. He bought people out for thirty years and keeps nothing for himself, though one year a berth-master paid coin and a season became two. I do not ask you to hate him. I ask you for the tokens."

New objective: Speak to Heavy-Rope at the head of Soulrest's dock.

content.content:
Heavy-Rope: "Then hear the plan, and better it if you can. When the Broker bought a person out of an Owing, he carved a token for them and kept it in his chest. A person has it back when they have worked a season's hire for him. My crew worked theirs and another. The tokens are still in the chest. The chest is in the north one of the three Dock Houses, up from the head of the dock where I stand. The old man sits in his room by it, and the key hangs on his belt. Feldril Nethri, a Dunmer labourer working off his own months, bars the north door. He might leave it unbarred for coin or a good word. A season is paid for by Ra'Jhan, the Khajiit berth-master, who keeps the shore at the landward end of the dock. He pays when it is sailed. Without him there is no season. The old man says the hire is promised to the price of eleven people held at Thorn, where it is worst. Hear my side. A last season that becomes two is an Owing with a new name, and we were promised an ending. If the old man wins, my crew row again and I do not know where it stops. Hear his. If we win, the eleven stay at Thorn. I will not tell you he is a bad man. He freed me. Lift the key or talk the door open, or go to Ra'Jhan. Whatever you do in that house, the old man is in the room, and if he sees you, you are a thief."
Objective completed: Speak to Heavy-Rope at the head of Soulrest's dock.
Journal entry (The Broker's Mercy): Heavy-Rope told me the tokens are in the Broker's chest, in the north one of the three houses by the dock. The old man keeps the key on his belt, and Feldril Nethri keeps his door. The berth-master Ra'Jhan pays for the season when it is sailed. I'm to free the crew by one of the three.
New objective: Free the crew: take the tokens from Ussa-Rekh's chest (his key, or the lock; Feldril Nethri keeps his door), or win Ussa-Rekh's word, or end Ra'Jhan's hire. Bring Never-Sold the book with her name on it from Ussa-Rekh's shelf.

content.content:
Ussa-Rekh: "Because the last season is not mine to spend. Ra'Jhan, the berth-master, pays this season's hire when it is sailed, and all of it is promised to the price of eleven people held at Thorn. Thorn is the saltrice country in the north-east of Black Marsh, and it is where an Owing is held hardest. Their names are on my table. I know of no other buyer for them, and I fear there is none. Heavy-Rope's crew have worked their season and one more. I know what that is, and I will not call it just. If they are freed now, the eleven stay at Thorn, and I do not know who else will ever pay for them. Carry that to the crew. Heavy-Rope is out on the dock. I would have him hear it from you."

One year a berth-master paid me for the whole season of a freed crew, and it bought twenty people out at once. A berth-master is the man who finds hands for the ships at a dock. I remember that year. == Four Months for a Boat (completed)
- Never-Sold of the Chainbreakers asked me to end Rows-For-Another's Owing on the Tulm-Varo estate: eleven years for one holed boat. She gave me a leaf in her own hand to leave in the count-box for the real one, five lockpicks, and 100 gold, the Owing's first price. I'm to speak to Rows-For-Another on the channel bank north of the farm.
- Rows-For-Another told me what holds her: her leaf in the count-box inside the estate house, whose key the keeper Hulm-Tei wears; Hulm-Tei's word, which could close the Owing; and Brings-Them-Back, the fetcher on the channel north of the bank, who knows the way to her home tree. I'm to break any one of the three.
- I killed Brings-Them-Back where the channel runs on north of the bank. Nobody living knows the way to Rows-For-Another's home tree now, to fetch her back from it. I'm to tell her the channel is clear, unless I end it another way first.
- I told Rows-For-Another the channel is clear. She will go by it once I have gone, and she gave me a word for Never-Sold. I'm to tell Never-Sold she is going.
- I told Never-Sold that Rows-For-Another has gone by the channel. Brings-Them-Back is dead, so nobody can follow her home, and her Owing will be written onto the keeper. Never-Sold paid me in full and named me one of the Chainbreakers, and did not thank me for how. She said to come back to her for more work.
== One Out of the Smoke (completed)
- Never-Sold sent me to the stone house on Blackrose's east shore, where the heirs of the Rose, the old prison a day south, keep three of their held. One of the three can be got out. She wants the one held for words, not the one held for a killing. I'm to speak to Third-Born Tsaxi, who keeps the post.
- I killed Third-Born Tsaxi at the heirs' post. Nobody is left to keep the three, so any of them can go, or all of them. I'm to tell them.
- I told Mends-Nets to go when I had gone. The other two stay. I'm to tell Never-Sold.
- I told Never-Sold that Mends-Nets came out. Walks-Far stays to work his three seasons, and Seven-Floods stays far from her Hist. Never-Sold said we will be called the people who loose killers, and that it will be true. She paid me 150 gold and said to come back to her for more work.

- Heavy-Rope will sail the last season, for the eleven at Thorn. He chose it himself, and bitterly. I'm to tell Never-Sold how it ended.
- I told Never-Sold that Heavy-Rope will sail the last season for the eleven at Thorn. The crew lose the ending they were promised. She named me a full Chainbreaker and gave me nothing else: "Eleven. input.command: /tmp/ptb-9i_lnhlm/play end --take 'I liked this. Never-Sold gives you jobs where every way out costs someone, and she says so to your face. The Broker quest was the best of the three. Ussa-Rekh is not a villain. Heavy-Rope calls him the man who freed him. Ra-Jhan, the berth-master, is just doing his job. I tried persuading Ra-Jhan and the Broker and failed, because I could not pay the 1000 gold. What worked was finding the list of the eleven names on the Broker table and showing it to Heavy-Rope, who then chose to sail the season himself. That felt like a real solution, not a lock to pick. It was a little odd that I had to steal the list in front of the Broker and nothing happened. The game says the fine or fight stage just is not implemented. I also never took Never-Sold book, and the quest finished anyway, so I do not know whether I was meant to. I understood who people were, and the Broker line about Never-Sold boat made me want to know their history. Earlier killings, Brings-Them-Back and Tsaxi, sat uneasily with the later story, and the game noticed that. Confusing parts: the door was locked Adept even though I was supposed to be able to talk my way in, and the tokens were never resolved. I do want to see what the Broker asks next, and what Thorn is like.'

Confusing parts: the door was locked Adept even though I was supposed to be able to talk my way in, and the tokens were never resolved. I do want to see what the Broker asks next, and what Thorn is like.'

I finished the third job, "The Broker's Mercy", and my journal has nothing active left. Never-Sold offers no further work for now.

**How it ended.** I never got the tokens. I showed Heavy-Rope the list of the eleven people held at Thorn, and he chose to sail one more season. The crew lose the ending they were promised. Never-Sold named me a full Chainbreaker and paid nothing.

**What I tried first.**
- **Ra'Jhan and the Broker:** persuading both failed. Paying them off would have cost 1000 gold, which I don't have.
- **The door:** I picked the Broker's lock, which was rated Adept.
- **The list:** I took it from the Broker's table while he was in the room. The game said I'd been seen and that the fine-or-fight step isn't implemented. Nothing happened to me.

**What I left undone.** I never took Never-Sold's book from the shelf, and the quest completed anyway.

I've submitted my take.
